answer_text:
Let

\[
I=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{\left(x^{3}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)^{2}}.
\]

Since \(x>0\),

\[
x^3+\frac1{x^3}=\frac{x^6+1}{x^3},
\]

so

\[
\frac{1}{\left(x^3+\frac1{x^3}\right)^2}
=\frac{x^6}{(x^6+1)^2}.
\]

Thus

\[
I=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{x^6}{(1+x^6)^2}\,dx.
\]

Now substitute \(t=x^6\). Then \(x=t^{1/6}\) and

\[
dx=\frac16 t^{-5/6}\,dt.
\]

Therefore

\[
I=\frac16\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{t^{1/6}}{(1+t)^2}\,dt.
\]

Rewrite the exponent as

\[
t^{1/6}=t^{\frac76-1},
\]

and note that

\[
2=\frac76+\frac56.
\]

So

\[
I=\frac16\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{t^{\frac76-1}}{(1+t)^{\frac76+\frac56}}\,dt.
\]

Using the beta-integral identity

\[
\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{t^{p-1}}{(1+t)^{p+q}}\,dt=B(p,q),
\]

with \(p=\frac76\) and \(q=\frac56\), we get

\[
I=\frac16 B\left(\frac76,\frac56\right).
\]

Now

\[
B\left(\frac76,\frac56\right)
=\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac76\right)\Gamma\left(\frac56\right)}{\Gamma(2)}.
\]

Since \(\Gamma(2)=1\) and \(\Gamma\left(\frac76\right)=\frac16\Gamma\left(\frac16\right)\),

\[
B\left(\frac76,\frac56\right)
=\frac16\Gamma\left(\frac16\right)\Gamma\left(\frac56\right).
\]

By Euler’s reflection formula,

\[
\Gamma\left(\frac16\right)\Gamma\left(\frac56\right)
=\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi/6)}
=2\pi.
\]

Hence

\[
B\left(\frac76,\frac56\right)=\frac16\cdot 2\pi=\frac{\pi}{3}.
\]

Finally,

\[
I=\frac16\cdot \frac{\pi}{3}
=\frac{\pi}{18}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{18}}
\]
